changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7313-object-calendar-record-source.md`

- names `plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectCalendar` resolves its records through the shared ladder (`resolveRecordSourceConfig` in `@object-ui/core`, called from `plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx`): `data` first, then `staticData`, then `objectName`. The published TypeScript interface REQUIRED `objectName` and declared neither `data` nor `staticData`; the published Zod mirror did the same. So an `object-calendar` node authored on `staticData` — the route the plugin page documents twice — rendered correctly and was refused by `safeValidateSchema`, and could not be annotated with its own type (`TS2741: Property 'objectName' is missing`).

- names `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` → `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` — edited by this change

  > **A widening.** A node authoring `staticData` or `data` without `objectName` now validates (it always rendered — the read is `resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema)`, keyed on the three). Every document that validated before still validates: `objectName` alone still parses, an empty one included, because presence is `!== undefined`. The one shape the refinement refuses (none of the three) was refused before too, at `objectName`. The two static-data examples in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` are now annotated `ObjectCalendarSchema` and compile under the doc-snippet gate.

### `.changeset/7712-kanban-calendar-filter-input.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectKanban.tsx` sends the authored key to the query as `$filter: schema.filter` and `ObjectCalendar.tsx` does the same, and `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap` declares `filter` on both blocks (measured: `safeParse` accepts it, and refuses an undeclared key by name on the same call). But none of the four registrations that publish those two renderers listed `filter` in `inputs`, and `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` reports `unknown-prop` for every key no `inputs` entry claims. So an author writing the one spelling that WORKS was told it was unknown — objectui#6678's shape, where a correct write draws the same diagnostic as a write that does nothing. That is worse than an inert key: it actively punishes the correct behaviour, and the honest response to it is to delete working metadata.

### `.changeset/8171-calendar-sort-input.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#7712's defect, one key over. `ObjectCalendar.tsx` lowers the authored key onto its own query as `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`, and `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['object-calendar']` declares `sort` (measured on 17.2.0: `safeParse({ objectName, sort })` returns `success: true`, while the same strict schema on the same call refuses `bogusProp` by name — that control is what makes the acceptance a verdict). But neither of the two registrations that publish this renderer — `plugin-calendar:object-calendar` and `view:calendar` — listed `sort` in `inputs`, and `sdui-parser`'s `validateTree` reports `unknown-prop` for every key no `inputs` entry claims. So an author writing the one spelling that WORKS was told it was unknown — objectui#6678's shape, where a correct write draws the same diagnostic as a write that does nothing.

### `.changeset/8174-kanban-calendar-filter-sort.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `filter` had four declaration faces and only three of them named it: `@objectstack/spec` declares it (`ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban']` and `['object-calendar']`), both plugins' registration `inputs` publish it, and both renderers read it — `ObjectKanban.tsx` lowers `schema.filter` onto `$filter`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx` lowers `schema.filter` onto `$filter` and `schema.sort` onto `$orderby` through `convertSortToQueryParams`. This package's own published faces (the TypeScript interface and its zod mirror) named none of them, so an authored value reached the renderer only through `BaseSchema`'s index signature and the mirror's `.passthrough()` — admitted, never examined. That is the same reasoning objectstack-ai/objectui#7322 used to move `groupBy` and `limit` into this same interface.

### `.changeset/8466-calendar-color-allday-fields.md`

- names `ObjectCalendar.tsx` → `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectCalendar.tsx`'s `getCalendarConfig` reads FIVE flat keys off the node, and `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` teaches all five in one sentence — "point `titleField` / `startDateField` / `endDateField` / `allDayField` / `colorField` at your own fields when they differ." Only three of the five were declared. The other two reached the renderer through `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` on the TypeScript face and its `.passthrough()` on the zod mirror: admitted, never examined. A misspelling therefore left the calendar silently colourless while every published gate passed.

- names `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` → `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `ObjectCalendar.tsx`'s `getCalendarConfig` reads FIVE flat keys off the node, and `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md` teaches all five in one sentence — "point `titleField` / `startDateField` / `endDateField` / `allDayField` / `colorField` at your own fields when they differ." Only three of the five were declared. The other two reached the renderer through `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any` on the TypeScript face and its `.passthrough()` on the zod mirror: admitted, never examined. A misspelling therefore left the calendar silently colourless while every published gate passed.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e327c8998` (merge-base with origin/main): 7 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1714 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2318 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36514895770)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `600e84cb52cab4b9e59d956a86e3c3ed0421233a`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #11005 (body; comments 5874661711 decision-box, 5881826705 ruling B, 5882077455 claim, 5882783174 os-dev-report), PR #11036 (body, nine-file list, net diff against `main`), the 43 check-runs on the head (40 success; 3 skipped conditional lanes: coverage, coverage shard, dependabot; none failed, none pending), plus `contents` reads at the head for context only: `CalendarView.tsx`, `ObjectCalendar.tsx`, `.changeset/10866-calendar-gantt-date-only-days.md`, `vitest.config.mts`, the root listing. Nothing built, run or re-run.

1. **Month-grid `move` — RIGHT.** `MonthView.handleDrop` now counts `calendarDaysBetween(anchorDay, newTargetDay)` (difference of local Y/M/D taken on the UTC calendar, so always a whole number) and applies `moveByCalendarDays` (`setDate` on a copy) to the start and to the end. That is the ruled form in 5881826705: the calendar days between the grab cell and the drop cell, applied with `setDate` on a local copy, hours / minutes / seconds untouched. Public surface: the instants `CalendarViewProps.onEventDrop` receives from a month-view drag change across a DST change (10:00 stays 10:00; a local-midnight start lands at midnight of the dropped day). Ruled, deliberate, and stated in the changeset. The legacy no-`sourceDay` fallback (anchor at the event's start day) is preserved.
2. **Month-grid `resize-end` — RIGHT.** The end moves by `calendarDaysBetween(oldEnd, newTargetDay)` through `moveByCalendarDays`; the start is handed back unchanged; the two guards (same cell, drop before the start day) are kept. Read at the head: the handle renders only where `isSpanEnd`, and `eventsByDate` puts that on the end's own local day (a midnight end included), so the grabbed cell is the end's day and the ruling's grab-cell-to-drop-cell wording holds for the end drag. Milliseconds are now kept where the old `setHours(h, m, s, 0)` zeroed them: a consequence of the ruled `setDate`-on-a-copy form, not an addition.
3. **`ObjectCalendar` day repair removed — RIGHT.** `toMovedDateValue`, `isStoredDay` and `DAY_MS` are deleted (all module-private; no export touched) and the default drop handler writes through `toStoredDateValue` again. A `date` read at local midnight (`toDisplayDate`) and moved by `setDate` stays at local midnight of the dropped day, and `toStoredDateValue` writes its local day: the same day the repair wrote. The ruling's condition ("removed once measured redundant") is met: slice 4's ten day moves in `ObjectCalendar.dstDayMove-10866` are untouched and green on the head, and the dev's ablation (base grid put back with the repair still gone: four Los Angeles day moves red) shows B is what makes it redundant.
4. **Week and day views unchanged — RIGHT.** The ruling has them ride only if their drop arithmetic is the same elapsed-time form. Read at the head: `TimeGridView`'s move places the start with `setHours(0, snapped)` on the drop column's own day, and its two resizes with `setHours(0, minutes)` on that day; there is no two-midnights `deltaMs`. Not the ruled form, so not riding is the correct reading. (Its end is `newStart` plus `durationMin` in milliseconds, a same-day duration form; see ③.)
5. **Ruled zone pins — RIGHT and complete.** New `CalendarView.monthMoveCalendarDays-11005`: Los Angeles six moves and two end drags, including the card's exact case (Nov 1 00:00 PDT, grabbed on the 2nd, dropped on the 3rd, now Nov 2 00:00 PST); Shanghai four drags at exactly N x 24 h; two suite-zone cases; a rig case and a fixture-validity case per zone so a child whose zone did not move goes red. Registered in the driver's `PINS`; `scripts/**/*.test.ts` is in the root `unit` project, so the driver (which fails unless every pin ran and passed in a forks child) runs inside CI's Test shards, all success. The ruling's five pins map one to one: DST wall-clock kept; local-midnight instant lands on the dropped day; date-only unchanged (the ten day moves); zone without DST as before; `resize-end` under the same rule. The single changed expectation in `dstDayMove-10866` (first Los Angeles `datetime` control's end, 09:00 to 10:00 PST on Nov 2) is exactly the ruled instant change; every other expectation there is untouched.
6. **Docs (README gesture table, plugin mdx month-view bullets) — RIGHT.** Prose only; each states the ruled behaviour (time of day kept for a move and for an end drag).
7. **No other public-surface movement.** `export { CalendarView }` and the test-only export are unchanged; no prop, type or config accept set moves. README Export Check success.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11005-month-grid-calendar-days.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-calendar': patch` — RIGHT. The diff publishes a behaviour fix inside one released package with no API added, removed or re-signed; the ruling prices it patch. Its prose matches the diff (move; end drag including milliseconds; `date` fields through the repair's removal; week and day views unchanged). Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read and Changeset Overwrite Report: all success on the head.
- Reconciliation — RIGHT. `.changeset/10866-calendar-dst-day-moves.md` (slice 4) carried two sentences this diff falsifies ("The month grid moves each date of an event by the milliseconds…" and "the grid's own arithmetic does not change"); both are now scoped "at this change" with a dated note naming objectui#11005; the front matter is untouched (the hunk starts at line 7) and the gantt and core bullets are untouched. The order's named file, `.changeset/10866-calendar-gantt-date-only-days.md` (slice 1), read at the head: its "A `datetime` field keeps its instant" sits under Writes and describes the type split (instant, not day), which the ruling itself says still governs the binding; no sentence there is falsified, so leaving it untouched is right.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body — RIGHT; it matches the ruling's execution parameter and the claim's reading: the written instant changes by ruling, and no declared field shape, schema or accept set moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (`deviations` in os-dev-report 5882783174), each answered:

1. File-surface additions (driver `PINS` entry; `packages/plugin-calendar/README.md`; `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx`) — ACCEPTED. The `PINS` entry is the only way the `runIf(DRIVEN)` zone cases run at all, so it is part of "zone pins under Los Angeles and Shanghai"; the two docs are prose under the repo's docs-driven rule. Neither `plugin-gantt` nor an objectui#10866 slice-5 item is touched: both of the claim's ⛔ bounds hold.
2. Reconciled slice 4's changeset rather than the named slice-1 file — ACCEPTED (see ②): the named file is not falsified and the slice-4 file was; the conditional's purpose, that no false pending sentence ships, is served.
